gaps.sentence: He ___ spend so much time on his phone; it is affecting his sleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't' advises against an action: shouldn't spend.

gaps.sentence: Sorry I am late — I ___ to take my car to the garage this morning.
gaps.explanation: Past obligation uses 'had to', since 'must' has no past form: had to.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have received your email — her inbox was full last week.
gaps.hint: ruled out as a past possibility
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' plus the participle rules out a past possibility: can't have received.

gaps.sentence: You have been travelling all day, so you ___ be exhausted.
gaps.hint: an obvious conclusion from known facts
gaps.explanation: A logical conclusion from known facts uses 'must': must be exhausted.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: Her car is not in the car park and her office light is off, so she ___ home.
gaps.hint: a confident conclusion about the past
gaps.explanation: A confident conclusion about the past uses 'must have' plus the participle: must have gone.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to see that exhibition before it closes — it is outstanding.
gaps.hint: a strong recommendation with ought to
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' recommends something strongly: ought to see.

gaps.sentence: You ___ pay for children under six — entry is free for them.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' expresses absence of necessity: needn't pay.
